results: The finite trace of every actual piecewise C1 loop is compact. A shared open-disc cut-period theorem encloses two arbitrary contours and the closed star-convex cut in one smaller closed disc. It proves the integral is a reference winding-one period multiplied by the ACTUAL winding, without analyticity at the original outer boundary.

The exact endpoint-root primitive period now holds for EVERY piecewise C1 loop in the full original open disc minus a COMPLEX segment. It equals minus d-squared/c times the sine-square mean times ACTUAL winding. A collapsed segment gives zero period by analytic extension. A genuine enclosing positive circle with winding one is constructed for every complex or collapsed segment inside the disc.

For the ACTUAL original high Hill discriminant/root integrand, every admissible contour has action (u-l)^2/(8*pi*n) times the normalized semicircle mean of the SAME intrinsic normalized root, times its actual midpoint winding. Thus any two contours of equal winding have equal actions for the same local square chart, with no shape or gap-reality assumption.

The exact error norm(8*pi*n*I-(u-l)^2)<=norm(u-l)^2*epsilon now holds for ALL COMPLEX actual pairs and every admissible winding-one contour. ONE complex H-minus-one neighborhood and ONE cutoff work before ALL later indices and ALL COMPLEX nearby potentials. Realness is not assumed. Collapsed pairs remain included.

A shared LOCAL even-family square-descent theorem proves F(d(q),q) analytic from joint analyticity of F at the actual input, global evenness in d and analyticity of d(q)^2. The chosen root d may be discontinuous and may vanish. The proof reuses the existing verified fixed-Cauchy-circle square descent and local analytic square roots.

The normalized sine-square cosine mean is even in its complex half-gap. Shared Banach-parameter interval integration gives joint analyticity from regularity along the ACTUAL cosine segment only; local even-family square descent then proves analyticity through collapse without selecting an analytic endpoint ordering or enclosing an entire open gap in an extra analytic disc.

Values of the ACTUAL intrinsic monic gap polynomial at zero and one recover an analytic midpoint and analytic squared half-gap. They equal (l+u)/2 and ((u-l)/2)^2 for EVERY actual multiplicity-counted pair. The native normalized action ratio is their EVEN semicircle mean of the actual intrinsic root, using a principal square-root selection whose sign/regularity cancels.

hillHminusNormalizedActionRatio is analytic on the original OPEN COMPLEX H-minus-one source neighborhood, including EVERY collapsed high gap, and is independent of endpoint ordering within the actual local polynomial. EVERY actual winding-one local contour satisfies I=(u-l)^2*R/(8*pi*n), with the EXACT original unit-period normalization. No division by the gap is used to define or prove analyticity of R.

For EVERY native COMPLEX q there exists ONE radius; for EVERY epsilon>0 there exist ONE OPEN COMPLEX neighborhood and ONE cutoff before ALL high n and ALL COMPLEX inputs. Their SAME actual square gives an analytic intrinsic R with norm(R-1)<=epsilon and R!=0, an actual winding-one contour, exact factorization for EVERY admissible winding-one contour and I=0 IFF the ACTUAL pair is collapsed.

These prove the complex analytic normalized ratio and zero-action equivalence for the CONSTRUCTED LOCAL HIGH contour actions. Independence across DIFFERENT local square/radius charts and identification with ONE global original canonical action family at ALL indices remain open; source3.2 is therefore not marked complete. The actual KdV Birkhoff map, actual smooth-approximation flow and all five MAIN theorems remain UNPROVED; goal ACTIVE.

The exact uniform bound is norm(R-1)<=epsilon for ALL COMPLEX nearby potentials. At collapse the factorization gives zero action; R remains analytic and is nonzero in the actual uniform construction.
